To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a method to map angular momentum states from the continuum to the lattice, and vice versa.

the mapping of angular momentum states to a lattice is given by the irreducible representations of the double cover with parity of the Euclidean space group, and the inverse mapping gives the degeneracy of the continuum angular momentum states in the limit of a vanishing lattice spacing.

the mapping of continuum rotational states to the lattice is done by subducing irreducible representations of the double cover group of the Euclidean Group with Parity to the corresponding cubic lattice space groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the application of the methods of group theory to the study of quantum mechanical problems in which the symmetry of the Hamiltonian is reduced to a finite subgroup by the introduction of a crystal lattice.
the application of group theory and symmetry principles in condensed matter physics and in particular in lattice dynamics.

the mapping of the irreducible representations (irreps) of the double-cover group of the Euclidean symmetry group (the Euclidean group with the addition of parity) to the irreps of the cubic space group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mapping between lattice and continuum angular momentum states is a many-to-one mapping.
the mapping of the continuum states to the lattice states is a one-to-one correspondence.
the angular momentum on the lattice is a very rich and complex problem that deserves to be studied in detail.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lattice states with non-zero momentum can be mapped to continuum angular momentum states, and the lattice IRs are the building blocks of continuum angular momentum.

we have found that the mapping of the continuum angular momentum IRs to the lattice IRs is given by the little groups of the momentum vectors on the lattice, and that the lattice IRs of the double cover group with parity decompose into the IRs of its little groups.
the lattice states with a given momentum and angular momentum are obtained by the reduction of the corresponding continuum IRs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lattice angular momentum states are the result of the mapping between the continuum states and the lattice states with the corresponding linear momentum.
the continuum angular momentum states can be mapped onto the lattice in a way that respects the symmetries of the lattice, which can be exploited in numerical simulations of lattice field theories.
the lattice IRs can be used to classify the continuum states, which is a useful tool for the study of the lattice Hamiltonian.
